chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Halabi and al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Thaqafi, all from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) finished the last Isha prayer, he would retire to his bed and not pray anything except after the middle of the night, neither in the month of Ramadan nor in other months.' The meaning in these narrations and those that follow the same pattern is that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray the voluntary prayer in congregation during the month of Ramadan. And if there were goodness in it, he would not have left it (peace be upon him and his family). And he did not mean that it is impermissible to pray individually. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.بَعْدَ انْتِصَافِ اللَّيْلِ: after the middle of the night

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) pray voluntary prayers in congregation during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to resolve the apparent contradiction between the Prophet’s (SAW) consistent individual night prayers and the later establishment of Taraweeh in congregation, arguing that his omission of congregational voluntary prayers in Ramadan was a matter of personal preference (sunna) rather than prohibition. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for validating the practice of praying Taraweeh in congregation while maintaining that the Prophet’s specific habit does not invalidate the communal form. The text explicitly notes that this individual practice occurred both in Ramadan and other months, emphasizing the flexibility of voluntary worship.
